name: Jikowood
tagline: Showcase and portfolio for a custom carpentry workshop in Brussels: 100+ project photos, three languages, client reviews and local SEO
role: A carpentry workshop sells through photos. For this Brussels client I designed and built jikowood.be end to end: a filterable portfolio of 17 custom projects, a page per project, reviews in a database, a contact form and a FR/EN/NL interface. The challenge: serve ~106 HD photos without slowing the site, and be found locally on Google. Live since January 2025, evolved for a year with new jobs (177 commits, 11 reviews, 81 sitemap URLs).

meta.title: Jikowood · Case study
meta.description: Brussels carpentry showcase: photo portfolio, local SEO, i18n and reviews in a database.

paragraphs: Custom carpentry is not a catalog product: it sells craft, proven by real projects. Someone looking for a walk-in closet or TV unit wants concrete interiors before requesting a quote.
Immediate technical problem: a credible portfolio is ~100 HD photos, and heavy photos bounce mobile visitors. The site had to stay fast while showing a lot.

It also had to be found. In Brussels the same prospect may search in French, Dutch or English. Ranking for local queries matters more than a campaign. And the client needed to add reviews without calling me every time.
Built around projects. Home: About, Services, Work, Reviews, Contact. Filterable portfolio and slug pages that are shareable and indexable.
SEO in sprint one: 15 Jan Open Graph, sitemap, robots; 16 Jan dedicated SEO pass. LocalBusiness JSON-LD for local results.
Reviews in MongoDB instead of hardcoding: client adds them without redeploy (1-5 rating, approval status). Projects stay static files: fastest to serve, rarely change.

context.title: Product context
paragraphs: Typical visitor: homeowner with a fit-out project. Arrives from search or a shared link, browses similar work, reads reviews, requests a quote.
Short visual journey: see, trust, contact. Form via Web3Forms, no mail server to maintain.
Basic offline mode (service worker + offline.html), Vercel Analytics and Speed Insights.

architecture.title: Architecture
paragraphs: Front: Next.js 14 App Router by screen. framer-motion animations, Swiper carousels. Locale in Zustand, copy in three JSON dictionaries.
Images are the performance core. WebP sources; next/image serves AVIF/WebP with sizes 640–3840. sharp processing, critical CSS via critters, JS bundle splitting.
Back: API route for MongoDB reviews via Mongoose. 17 static projects. HTTPS + HSTS and restrictive security headers.

decisions.title: Key decisions
paragraphs: Client kept seeing an old version after photo updates (browser/CDN/build cache). Fixed 4 Apr in five commits: timestamped generateBuildId, Cache-Control for HTML revalidation, image versioning from March. In hindsight only HTML and replaced images need revalidation; hashed assets can cache for a year.
Keep portfolio richness and optimize the pipeline (WebP, modern formats, responsive sizes, 24h optimized-image cache, lazy load).
Local discovery: LocalBusiness JSON-LD, metadata, Open Graph, hreflang sitemap. SEO passes in February and April.
bullets: Reviews in DB: content without pinging me
Static projects: most viewed content is fastest
Web3Forms: no email infra for a brochure site
Next security bump to 14.2.35 in December 2025

execution.title: Delivery and next steps
paragraphs: 7-16 Jan 2025: initial sprint. February: SEO. March: new projects, image versioning. April: cache, build id, refactor, new photos. May: new job. December 2025: Next security fix and redeploy.
Numbers: 177 commits, 4 pages, 2 API routes, 17 projects, ~106 photos, 11 reviews, 3 languages, 81 sitemap URLs, ~6k lines.

Honesty: first client site in production, maintained a year. What I would strengthen (and a rewrite targets): server title/meta on home, real per-locale URLs so the sitemap stops pointing at 404s, manual review approval, long cache on static assets, TypeScript everywhere, tests and CI.
